profile.headline: Orthopoxvirus causing mpox; clade I is more virulent, clade II drove the 2022 global outbreak through sexual networks.
profile.syndrome: Fever, lymphadenopathy (a feature distinguishing it from smallpox-like illness without nodes) and a deep-seated vesiculopustular rash, often anogenital and oropharyngeal in sexually transmitted clade IIb infection. Proctitis, severe pain and bacterial superinfection are common; severe disease occurs in advanced HIV.
profile.transmission: Close skin-to-skin and sexual contact, respiratory secretions on prolonged contact, fomites, vertical transmission, and zoonotic contact with rodents.
profile.reservoir: African rodents (squirrels, dormice); primates are incidental hosts despite the name.
profile.geography: Endemic in Central and West Africa; global clade IIb outbreak since 2022 and clade Ib expansion from eastern DRC since 2023.
profile.diagnosis: PCR on lesion swabs (the specimen of choice).
profile.management: Supportive with pain control; tecovirimat showed no efficacy for clade I lesion resolution in the PALM007 trial, tempering earlier expectations.
profile.prevention: MVA-BN (JYNNEOS/Imvanex) vaccination pre- and post-exposure; isolation of lesions.
evidence: Tens of thousands of PCR-confirmed cases with detailed transmission-network epidemiology.

Vaccinia virus. Vaccine strain; causes progressive vaccinia, eczema vaccinatum and buffalopox.

profile.headline: Cause of smallpox — the only human disease ever eradicated (certified 1980). Retained only in two WHO-authorised repositories.
profile.syndrome: Variola major: prodromal fever, then a synchronous centrifugal vesiculopustular rash with ~30% case fatality; haemorrhagic and flat forms were almost uniformly fatal.
profile.transmission: Respiratory droplets and contact with lesion material or contaminated linen.
profile.reservoir: Humans only — which is why eradication was achievable.
profile.diagnosis: Historical: electron microscopy, culture. Now PCR in reference laboratories only.
profile.management: Historically supportive; tecovirimat and brincidofovir are stockpiled against re-emergence.
profile.prevention: Vaccinia-based vaccination; ring vaccination and surveillance-containment achieved eradication.
evidence: Definitive — the eradication programme is the canonical demonstration of a single-host human pathogen.
